handz_fight_tips: Hitting an opponent in the green-zone of their rhythm will leave them vulnerable to stun, crit, and extra damage.
Changing your rhythm makes it harder for your opponent to hit you when you're the most vulnerable.
Punching on either side of your rhythm grants a damage boost.
Getting Stunned pauses rhythm, and lowers speed temporarily.
Ducking can help you evade head punches, but pauses stamina recovery (unless your refinement is unlocked).
Ducking + Uppercut = BIG Power. Use strategically.
The opponent will try to time their punches to hit you when you're most vulnerable.
Stunning has a chance to lower your opponent's Knockdown recovery chance.
Timing a perfect Rhythm-Cut has a chance to wipe-out their charge punch bars.
The higher your speed stat, the lower the opponent's speed will seem mid-bout.
Raising your Focus stat boosts your chance for stuns and crits.
Heart Refinement increases stamina, recovery, and reduces stamina combo penalty.
Investing in the Duck Recovery Refinement grants the ability to duck while regaining stamina.
Power boosts Power, as well as damage multipliers.
Charge punch bar will build when clean hits land or are landed upon a fighter.
Charge punch must be landed shortly after loading with A, or else it will fail.
At Power 200, you are granted a max of 7 seconds to use your Charge Punch.
At Speed 200, movement speed and duck speed becomes significant.
At Stamina 200, punches cost less stamina to throw, and stamina recovery improves significantly.
At Defense 200, your Autoguard lasts almost an entire round.
Attacking or Feinting to the head will make your opponent expect it more often.
Ducking too much makes your opponent aim lower.
Stop guarding, punching, or moving for 1 second, and your stamina recovery speed raises.
After inactivity, the opponent will see you as a sitting duck.
When the opponent's stamina is low, they likely won't engage with you much.
A fighter getting Rhythm-Cut has a 30% chance to lower their max stamina next round by 1% (this stacks).
Hitting a fighter off balance, between the green vulnerability range of their rhythm, is called a Rhythm-Cut.
The cross does more damage when you aren't ducking.
Stamina recovery speed increases when your guard is lowered, but you're more vulnerable to crits.
Spamming jabs occasionally is a good way to create distance.
Don't spam combos too often, your stamina will drain faster after a few too many extra punches.
Each opponent has subtle differences in how they prefer to beat you.
Be cautions of an opponent feinting, they are looking to hit you with a Rhythm-Cut in the near future.
Charge Punches can stack with stuns and crits, if you can time it correctly, and get lucky.
Refinement gets cheaper in the postgame, so don't worry if you can't afford it now.
After a certain amount of training completions, you may unlock a previously locked stat for that training.
Focus and Stamina stats will drop after 6 weeks of not Sparring.
Power and Defense will drop after 6 weeks of not Weightlifting.
Speed will drop after 6 weeks of not training Heavy Bag.
Try to switch your aggression repeatedly, back off, repeat.
While it's incredibly hard to beat a much higher level opponent, you can technically win a round against them if you're skilled, or lucky.
Stamina IS health, just like a real boxing match. No stamina = No Handz being thrown.
Press V to perform a perfect block, tricky to time but blocks almost all damage.
Performing a Perfect Block (V) will lower the attacker's stamina by half their blocked punch's stamina cost, and pause stamina recovery for 2 seconds.
Every round that passes grants fatigue; max stamina is whittled down at the beginning of every round.
If a fighter is being out-landed, out-damaged, and outclassed, the ref or the fighter's corner may just end the fight early.
Use the settings gear in the career hub to set the clock and rounds.
Go through Tutorial mode! The game will be way simpler to grasp.
Every fighter has different availability. Negotiating gets easier the higher your rank becomes.
You may reschedule a couple fights for a guaranteed date a couple times per career.
If you reallocate points but use them all for Stat Refinement, you can re-convert them for a drop in rank.
Check your career stats toward the bottom of the Career Hub.
Check the roster at the bottom of the Career Hub.
Doghouse Rounds take awhile, so clear your schedule before starting.
Nightmare mode is a great way to practice distance management and effective power punching.
Doghouse Rounds grant lots of stat points, but the fighters you face have extreme endurance.
Nightmare mode brings in stronger fighters every so often, so be prepared to go through heck.
After beating the Champion, your level cap and stat caps are broken, but the same goes for your opponents.
Each fight you win grants a permanent EXP boost to all training.
Sparring partners have comparable stats to your own.
During Fight Camp weeks, Sparring partners have similar stats to your opponent, but typically aren't as strong overall.
If you find that your opponents are too weak, reroll your opponents.
In Orthodox vs Southpaw fights, jabs have a 10% more chance to be blocked, but do 12%  more damage.
In Orthodox vs Southpaw matches, throwing a cross punch has a 20% reduced block chance.
Throwing a hook while standing upright deals +10% damage in Orthodox vs Southpaw matches.
At career player level 50, you can switch stance mid-fight using Right Shift.
Switching stances mid fight has a chance to raise or lower your opponents' rhythm speed.
